notes: The session's web search allowance was already used up when this part began (every search was refused), so nothing here came from a search engine. Everything was found by reading known addresses directly: the campaign websites already filed with the Secretary of State (read from sl_websites in the database, opened read-only), each government's own site, the Minnesota DFL's endorsed-candidates page and the Legislative Reference Library. Pages were read with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), each site's robots.txt checked first; two were read with the fetch tool instead, as said below. Candidates with no entry are the ones this left out of reach.
Brock Ray (New Hope council, special election): the website he filed, brockfornewhope.com, asks scripts to stay out (robots.txt), so it was not read and nothing is recorded.

Stephen Knudsen and Jesse Vavreck: their filed sites answered the kit's reader 429 three times and answered the fetch tool normally; only the title and the office named are recorded. JD Delgado's filed site answered 503 to both; his website is tied to the race by the state DFL's page, which links it.

JD Delgado: the state DFL's page writes the endorsed House District 57A candidate as "Jenaro Delgado" and links jdformn.com, the address JD Delgado filed; a verifier should confirm they read this as the same person.

David H. Senjem: the Library's record also carries personal details (family, religion) that were not recorded. Three earlier appointed posts it lists without dates (Minnesota Emergency Response Commission, Olmsted County Environmental Commission, Rochester Park Board) were left out for want of years.

Not found on their governments' own pages (so nothing recorded): Annette Deyo (Winona County Recorder page), Traci Dawn Kamish (Crystal council page), Jordan Graen (Lake Elmo council page), Del Rae Williams (Moorhead's current mayor and council page), Ted Hazelton (Winona Area Public Schools board and Election 2026 pages), Stephen Knudsen (Douglas County Attorney's page). Roger Bovee appears only on Monticello schools' list of 2026 candidates, which says nothing more. New Ulm's and Marshall's school board pages showed no names to a script (Tara Nilson, Nathan Green); Hastings schools' board page asks scripts to stay out, and Wabasha County was not asked because part 10 found it does too (Jessica Dressely, Cindy McGrath). The Minnesota Judicial Branch site refuses scripts (noted by part 10), so Christina M. Wietzema was not looked up there.

Thomas J. Sexton and John Burkel are sitting legislators with roster records. Sexton filed no website and none was found without a search. No Republican unit's own page naming an endorsement for Burkel, Sexton or Luke Doerer was found; Burkel's own site says he is the Republican endorsed candidate (own_words).

No party endorsement was found for any nonpartisan office in this part: none of the county, city, park or school candidates appears on the Minnesota DFL's endorsed-candidates page, and Amanda McFarlane's endorsements page names no party in the text a script can read.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address was opened again (the fetch tool, or the kit's reader where the router lost the lookup). Two county addresses had moved and were corrected (Marshall, Norman). JD Delgado's website was removed because the site answered 503 on both tries; his endorsement stays, tied by House District 57A, the DFL label and the filed address the party links.
